Sinclair Lewis, Babbitt.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/sinclair-lewis/babbitt

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Sinclair Lewis, the author, died 1951 (Wikidata Q123469; death 1951-01-10 in the facts file).

First publication of the text used: 1922 (SE colophon: 'Babbitt was published in 1922 by Sinclair Lewis')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1922, before 1931, and the edition's rights statement below says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (not fixed by the facts): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Every person whose words are in the text died in 1955 or earlier, and nothing in the facts points to France, Spain, Mexico, Colombia or Russia/USSR. Each of the possible countries has a term of life + 70 years or shorter for these deaths, so the text is public domain in each of them, whichever one is the country of first publication, and simultaneous publication in two of them changes nothing.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
